paper.title_en: Revisiting Metastable Dark Energy in Light of DESI DR2 BAO and DESI DR1 Full-Shape Measurements
paper.abstract_en: We revisit metastable dark energy (DE) models described by a radioactive-like decay law. We consider three scenarios: an effective, exponentially decaying DE component; decay of DE into non-baryonic dark matter (DM); and decay of DE into dark radiation (DR). We constrain the metastable DE models using DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, Type Ia supernovae (SNIa), cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations, and, for the first time, the current available DESI DR1 full-shape (FS) clustering measurements. The BAO+SNIa combinations show a mild preference for positive $Γ/H_0$, with a deviation from the $Λ$CDM limit at the $\gtrsim 2σ$ level. This corresponds to a decaying DE density and an effective quintessence-like behaviour at low redshift. Once CMB information from either Planck or P-ACT is included, however, the constraints become statistically consistent with $Γ/H_0=0$. The FS measurements probe the growth sector and help distinguish the interacting DM-DE behaviour of Model 2 from the effective decaying-DE response of Model 1 and the weaker DR-induced response of Model 3. For CMB+FS+DES-Dovekie, Model 1 shows a slight deviation from $Γ/H_0=0$ at the $\gtrsim 2σ$ level, while Models 2 and 3 remain consistent with the $Λ$CDM limit within $2σ$. Overall, metastable DE remains phenomenologically viable: current data allow late-time dynamics but do not provide decisive evidence for a nonzero decay rate. These results motivate extending our analysis to the upcoming DESI DR2 FS data to obtain tighter constraints on metastable dynamics.
